problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must assign a series of shipments to identical freight trucks. The cargo manifests are as follows:

* Shipment Alpha: cargo mass 64 metric tons
* Shipment Beta: cargo mass 50 metric tons
* Shipment Gamma: cargo mass 68 metric tons
* Shipment Delta: cargo mass 42 metric tons
* Shipment Epsilon: cargo mass 65 metric tons
* Shipment Zeta: cargo mass 32 metric tons
* Shipment Eta: cargo mass 44 metric tons
* Shipment Theta: cargo mass 58 metric tons
* Shipment Iota: cargo mass 70 metric tons
* Shipment Kappa: cargo mass 62 metric tons
* Shipment Lambda: cargo mass 56 metric tons
* Shipment Mu: cargo mass 38 metric tons
* Shipment Nu: cargo mass 65 metric tons
* Shipment Xi: cargo mass 64 metric tons
* Shipment Omicron: cargo mass 32 metric tons
* Shipment Pi: cargo mass 42 metric tons
* Shipment Rho: cargo mass 48 metric tons
* Shipment Sigma: cargo mass 65 metric tons
* Shipment Tau: cargo mass 43 metric tons
* Shipment Upsilon: cargo mass 46 metric tons
* Shipment Phi: cargo mass 33 metric tons
* Shipment Chi: cargo mass 62 metric tons
* Shipment Psi: cargo mass 53 metric tons
* Shipment Omega: cargo mass 48 metric tons
* Shipment AA: cargo mass 54 metric tons
* Shipment BB: cargo mass 38 metric tons
* Shipment CC: cargo mass 32 metric tons
* Shipment DD: cargo mass 42 metric tons
* Shipment EE: cargo mass 69 metric tons
* Shipment FF: cargo mass 49 metric tons
* Shipment GG: cargo mass 43 metric tons
* Shipment HH: cargo mass 58 metric tons
* Shipment II: cargo mass 48 metric tons
* Shipment JJ: cargo mass 30 metric tons
* Shipment KK: cargo mass 32 metric tons

Each truck has a maximum cargo capacity of 100 metric tons. The coordinator must assign every shipment to exactly one truck, ensuring the combined mass in any truck does not surpass its limit, while utilizing the smallest possible number of trucks.
